extDescription.message: Estimates how much of your Claude usage limit a message will use before you send it, and suggests a cheaper model when one fits.

noData.message: No usage data yet. Open claude.ai while signed in.

bottleneck.message: This limit will run out first

fetchError.message: Couldn't read usage. Make sure you're signed in to claude.ai.

ctxOver.message: This won't fit in Claude's context window. Send only the parts you need.

ctxNear.message: This may not fit in Claude's context window. Consider splitting it or starting a new chat.

pdfTextOnly.message: PDF over 100 pages: Claude reads its text only, not images or charts.

pdfTooLarge.message: PDF over 1000 pages: claude.ai won't accept it.

warnNoFit.message: This will likely not fit in your $1 ($2 left).

warnMaybeFit.message: This might not fit in your $1 ($2 left).

ctxWorkspace.message: On paid plans claude.ai may move a very large file into a workspace instead, where Claude reads it with code rather than all at once.

warnCacheCold.message: You haven't used this chat for $1 min, so the cache has expired: the whole history (~$2 tokens) will count again. A new chat may be much cheaper.

warnCacheUnknown.message: If this chat was idle for over an hour, its history (~$1 tokens) will count again.

tipNewChat.message: This chat is long (~$1 tokens). Starting a new chat with a short summary keeps answers sharper and cheaper.

warnPeak.message: Peak hours (weekdays $1–$2 your time): on claude.ai the 5-hour limit fills faster right now. Consider moving long tasks outside this window.

recDowngrade.message: $1 would likely be enough and use about $2% less of your limit.

recUpgrade.message: This looks demanding; $1 may give a noticeably better answer.

rec_short_qa.message: Short factual questions rarely need a large model.

rec_rewrite.message: Editing a given text is a light task.

rec_summarize.message: Summaries are a strength of lighter models.

rec_explain.message: Explanations are handled well by mid-size models.

rec_data_analysis.message: Standard analysis fits a mid-size model.

rec_file_create.message: Documents and decks fit a mid-size model.

rec_code_write.message: Everyday coding fits a mid-size model.

rec_code_fix.message: Most debugging fits a mid-size model.

rec_research.message: Routine research fits a mid-size model.

rec_math.message: Routine problems fit a mid-size model.

rec_hardest.message: This is among the hardest kinds of task.

effLower.message: Low effort is usually enough for this; high effort mostly adds hidden thinking tokens.

effRaise.message: For a hard problem like this, higher effort may be worth it.

footCalibrated.message: Learned from $1 of your messages · $2% landed inside the range.

footLearning.message: Still learning: estimates get sharper after a few messages.

cardIdleSub.message: 5-hour limit used so far. Start typing to see an estimate.

notifThresholdBody.message: Plan bigger tasks with the forecast before sending.

notifThresholdBodyHigh.message: Almost out: finish what's important first.

notifResetBody.message: You can continue where you left off.

freePlanWait.message: On the free plan, usage appears after you send your first message in claude.ai.

capSub.message: Roughly one of these, in a new chat with $1 (cautious estimate).

calNone.message: No measurements yet. Each message you send teaches the extension how your plan really behaves.

calFew.message: $1 measurements so far; a few more and estimates sharpen.

calSome.message: $1 measurements · $2% of actual values fell inside the forecast range.

privacyNote.message: Everything is computed in your browser. Message text never leaves your device.

hHookNoReply.message: no reply – reload the claude.ai tab

hHookReplaced.message: fetch was replaced by the site

hProbe.message: sends go to a different address

hSendWait.message: no message sent yet, or not detected

hSseNo.message: stream read but no usage data in it

hHint.message: If a row shows a problem, copy the log and send it to the developer.

advSaveDetail.message: This message will use about $1 of your limit; with $2 about $3 ($4% saving).

advSaveNext.message: $1 is enough for tasks like this, but don't switch in this chat

advSaveNextDetail.message: The chat history ($1 tokens) isn't in the new model's cache and would be re-read, so this message would cost more. Pick $2 when you start your next new chat.

advUpgrade.message: This may be hard for $1: $2 is recommended

advUpgradeDetail.message: $1 uses your limit about $2× as fast. If you'd rather try $3 first, upgrade if the answer falls short.

advOkTiny.message: $1 would also do, but the difference is tiny ($2 of your limit).

why_simple_task.message: A simple, clear task; the classifier is confident.

why_unsure_safe.message: I'm not sure about the task type, so I stay on the safe side and suggest at least Sonnet.

why_hardest.message: A very hard derivation, design or research task.

why_pref_floor.message: Based on your feedback I pick a stronger model for tasks like this.

why_pref_ceil.message: Based on your feedback I don't push a stronger model for tasks like this.

basis_haiku.message: Anthropic positions Haiku 5.5 as "the lowest latency and price" model, for high-volume, simple tasks and sub-agent work.

basis_sonnet.message: Per Anthropic, Sonnet 5.5 offers "speed and capability for everyday workloads": code generation, data analysis, content creation.

basis_opus.message: Anthropic recommends Opus 5.5 for complex coding and enterprise work: large refactors, systems engineering, multi-hour agents.

basis_fable.message: Fable 5.1 is "the highest available capability": multi-hour agent sessions, multistep deep research.

tbasis_short_qa.message: Single-answer factual questions need short replies; light models do them well. Questions about people or events can be made up — verify if it matters.

tbasis_translate.message: In translation the text is already there; the model keeps the meaning and changes the language. Light models do this well.

tbasis_rewrite.message: When editing or simplifying, the content is given; the model only improves the form.

tbasis_summarize.message: In a summary the information is in the text; a light model is fine for short texts, a mid model is safer for long or technical documents.

tbasis_explain.message: Explaining concepts needs accuracy and good examples; a mid model is usually enough, Opus helps on advanced topics.

tbasis_writing.message: For writing and emails, a mid model balances tone and fluency well.

tbasis_data_analysis.message: Data analysis mixes calculation and interpretation; a mid model is usually enough.

tbasis_file_create.message: Creating files or decks is multi-step work; a mid model is usually enough, Opus for long documents.

tbasis_code_write.message: Sonnet is strong at everyday coding; Opus is recommended for architecture and multi-file work.

tbasis_code_fix.message: Sonnet handles single-file bugs; Opus for hard or system-wide bugs.

tbasis_research.message: Research means finding and synthesizing sources; Opus or Fable for deep, multistep research.

tbasis_math.message: Calculations and standard problems suit a mid model; proofs and long derivations suit Opus or Fable.

when_haiku.message: Switch to Sonnet if the answer is shallow or wrong.

when_sonnet.message: Switch to Opus if the answer falls short or the task grows.

when_opus.message: Use Fable for multi-hour agent work or if Opus isn't enough.

when_fable.message: Fable is the strongest and most expensive model; use it only for truly hard tasks.

advCaveat.message: This suggestion is an estimate from rules plus a small learned model running on your device; answer quality was not measured. Your feedback and corrections tune it to you.

importReady.message: Backup read: $1 measurements ($2). It will replace what's learned now; press the button again to confirm.

importBad.message: This file isn't a valid Token Forecast backup.

cacheWarmLeft.message: warm · history free for $1 more min

cacheColdAgo.message: cold (last message $1 ago) · history is re-read

tipHandoff.message: This chat is long ($1 tokens) and grows with every message. To move to a new chat, you can ask Claude for a short handoff summary.

tipHandoffWarm.message: This chat is long ($1 tokens). Asking for a handoff summary is cheap while the cache is warm; paste it into a new chat and continue there.

handoffPrompt.message: I'm moving this conversation to a new chat. Write a short handoff summary: the goal, decisions made so far, important details (file names, numbers, code snippets), open questions and the next step. Make it ready to paste into a new chat, 300 words max.

warnSurprise.message: Your last message used more than expected: $1 (estimate $2). Possible reasons: $3.

cr_cold.message: you wrote after a long break, so the history was re-read

cr_long_answer.message: the answer was longer than expected

cr_elsewhere.message: the same account may have been used in another tab, device or Claude Code

rpSaveSub.message: a lighter model would have done for $1 messages

tip_peak.message: $1% of your usage happened at peak hours ($2, weekdays). claude.ai fills the 5-hour limit faster then; moving long tasks outside that window gets the same work done with less of your limit.

tip_cold.message: $1 messages went into a long chat after a break of more than an hour, so the whole history was re-read each time ($2% of your usage). After a break, a new chat or a handoff summary is cheaper.

tip_advice.message: A lighter model would have been enough for $2 messages. Following the suggestion would have saved about $1 of a session limit.

tip_long.message: $1 messages were sent in chats over 100K tokens. Context that long strains both your limit and answer quality; splitting topics into new chats helps.

tip_effort.message: High thinking effort was on for $1 simple tasks (translation, quick questions). Low effort gives the same result for less there.

tip_upgrade.message: A stronger model was suggested for $1 messages. If answers fell short, starting such tasks on the stronger model is cheaper than asking again and again.

tip_good.message: Your usage looks balanced this week: no clear problem with peak hours, long chats or oversized models.

rpHeat.message: When do you write? (last 4 weeks, your time)

rpAccVal.message: $2 of $1 measured messages fell within the forecast range.

rpAccNone.message: No measured messages this week; values are estimates.

rpMeasuredShare.message: $1 of the values were measured; the rest are send-time estimates.

rpPrivacy.message: This report is computed only in this browser, from records that contain no message text.

rpNoData.message: Not enough records for a report yet. After a few days of writing on claude.ai this page fills up.

setWeekly.message: Weekly report notification on Monday morning

burnEta.message: At the last hour's pace it fills around $1 (resets $2).

burnSafe.message: At this pace it won't fill before it resets.

burnIdle.message: No notable usage in the last hour.

advRelabel.message: Wrong task type? Pick the right one:

advRelabelThanks.message: Thanks — learning from this on this device.

comText.message: Sharing what was learned on this device makes forecasts accurate from day one for new users. The summary contains no message text, chat names, dates or account details. You see the content before sending; nothing is sent automatically.

comCopied.message: Copied. Paste it into the box in the form that opened and submit.

comNoUrl.message: Copied. The community form opens soon; you can keep the text for now.

comEmpty.message: Nothing to share yet. Try again after sending a few messages.

rpWeekLinePct.message: Last 7 days: $1 messages · $2 of 5-hour limits used in total

dbasis_science.message: In science, accuracy and consistency matter; detailed explanations get one effort level more.

dbasis_math.message: Math needs step-by-step reasoning; proofs and derivations get at least High effort.

dbasis_engineering.message: Mistakes in engineering calculations are costly; design and calculation work gets one effort level more.

dbasis_software.message: Effort rises with code complexity; for hard coding on Opus, Anthropic suggests trying Extra high first.

dbasis_data_ai.message: Data and AI tasks usually need moderate reasoning.

dbasis_academic.message: Consistency matters in academic text; edits usually need little effort, literature reviews and methods more.

dbasis_project.message: Anthropic recommends raising effort for project planning; planning gets at least Medium.

dbasis_literature.message: Long thinking rarely improves creative writing; effort is capped at Medium.

dbasis_business.message: Business writing is usually routine; the default or lighter setting is enough.

dbasis_finance.message: Wrong money advice can hurt: no light model, effort at least Medium.

dbasis_law.message: Wrong legal information can hurt: no light model, effort at least Medium. Ask a lawyer for important decisions.

dbasis_health.message: Wrong health information can hurt: no light model, effort at least Medium. In an emergency, see a doctor.

dbasis_education.message: Study tasks are mostly explanations; effort rises with difficulty.

dbasis_language.message: Language tasks (translation, grammar) are usually light; one effort level lower is enough.

dbasis_humanities.message: History and philosophy explanations need moderate reasoning.

dbasis_daily.message: Everyday tasks are light; one effort level lower is enough.

effLowerX.message: Setting effort to $1 saves about $2 of the limit on this message.

effAssumedNote.message: (Couldn't read the effort setting on the page; assumed the model default, $1.)

effRaiseX.message: Setting effort to $1 may give a more reliable answer for this task.

advEffLowerDetail.message: Now: $1. For this kind of task $2 effort usually gives the same answer; less hidden thinking cuts this message's cost by about $3%.

advEffRaiseTitle.message: Set effort to $1 for this task

advEffRaiseDetail.message: Now: $1. This task needs deep reasoning; $2 effort gives a more reliable answer but this message costs about $3% more. A weak answer means asking again, which costs more.

effBasis.message: Effort basis: per Anthropic, Low and Medium stretch usage on routine tasks, High is the best balance, Extra high is for long coding and agent work, Max for the deepest reasoning.

why_stakes.message: In high-stakes topics (health, law, money) I don't suggest a light model.

rpDomainNote.message: Topic is guessed on your device from the words in the message; no text is stored.

tip_effort_over.message: Effort was above the suggestion on $1 messages. The suggested setting would have used about $2 less of the limit.

tip_domain_save.message: Most of the saving potential is in $1: a lighter model would have done for $2 messages.

tip_domain_stakes.message: $1 messages were about health, law or money. I don't suggest a light model or Low effort there; for important decisions also ask an expert.

rpEffOver.message: Effort was above the suggestion on $1 messages (missed saving ≈ $2).

rpEffOk.message: Your effort settings look in line with the suggestions.

rpLearnFew.message: $1 measured messages so far. Every 10 measurements make one bar, and a trend shows after 30 (about $2 more messages).

rpLearnBetter.message: In the first measurements the predicted total limit was off by a factor of $1, in the latest ones by $2. The extension is learning you.

rpLearnSame.message: Forecast error is $1× in the first measurements and $2× in the latest: no clear change. If it was already accurate, that is expected.

rpLearnWorse.message: The latest measurements are further off ($2×) than the first ($1×). Using the same account on another device or in Claude Code disturbs measurement; if so, try resetting calibration.

rpLearnRange.message: Staying inside the forecast range: $1 in the first measurements, $2 in the latest (target about 80%).

rpLearnNote.message: Each bar is 10 consecutive measured messages. It shows how far the predicted total limit was from what was actually spent (1.00 = perfect). Percentages are rounded to whole numbers, so 10-message totals are used instead of single messages.

setTips.message: Show tips (cache, peak hours, long chats, handoff summary)

setExplain.message: Show the “why did it cost this much?” explanation

viewSimple.message: Simple: forecast and limit warnings only

viewNote.message: The simple view hides model and effort suggestions, tips and cost explanations. The forecast and warnings about limits and context size always stay.

warnLangLimited.message: Message analysis (task type, topic, model and effort advice) currently works for Turkish and English messages only. In this language you get the token and limit forecast, but no advice.

welLead.message: Before it starts, here is exactly what the extension reads and keeps. Nothing leaves your device.

welRead1.message: The text and attachments in the message box, to count tokens and estimate the cost. Not stored.

welRead2.message: The open chat's history, to calculate cache and context. Counted locally, not stored.

welRead3.message: Your 5-hour and weekly usage percentages, read from claude.ai with your own session.

welStoreTitle.message: What it keeps on this device

welStore.message: Your settings, learned numbers (such as your plan size) and a log of sends for the weekly report that contains only numbers and labels, never text. You can export it or reset it in Settings; uninstalling removes it.

welNever.message: No server, no analytics, no tracking. It never sends your messages anywhere, never sends messages for you and never changes your claude.ai settings.

welDone.message: All set. Go back to your claude.ai tab and start typing.

welLaterNote.message: The extension stays off until you agree. You can do this later from the extension window.
